correctness.rationale: A color class blocks all lines and contains no line. If a smaller class existed, it could be extended to a line-free five-set: at most four candidate points complete a collinear triple at each step. The five-point incidence equations require three trisecants, which together contain at least six class points. Six points instead force four trisecants; any pair must meet in the class or exhaust it, and no three concur. Thus the class is the six corners of a line frame. Conversely each frame has four trisecants, three bisecants and six unisecants, proving admissibility; the frame is recovered from the class. Exactly the four distinct missing frame-line points are forbidden additions. This gives cubic degree and the disjointness double-cover relation: disjoint six-sets leave one point to flip. Arc transitivity can also be checked without computation: take frame lines x=0, y=0, z=0, x+y+z=0; the three legal additions are the projective points with all coordinates nonzero and exactly one sign different, permuted transitively by the coordinate permutations. The fresh standard-library enumeration over 8192 labeled colorings and 715 four-line choices independently confirms the frame classification, both full graphs and all required metrics and stabilizer data; replay with python3 /workspace/branches/894eb9e5-e685-4e9b-a82b-59ab30dcfb1f/pg3_independent_reproduction.py (matching .out in that directory). It finds H connected and nonbipartite, girth 12 and diameter 8; R connected and bipartite, girth 12, 702 edges, diameter 13 and the claimed shell profile at all roots. Conder–Nedela's complete census distinguishes H from F234A, so this is not an unsupported fingerprint-isomorphism inference. The cited F468 bipartite double cover of the connected nonbipartite Wong graph is necessarily canonical: if one fiber were monochromatic in the bipartition, all would be by covering along paths, forcing the base bipartite; otherwise each fiber has one vertex in each part and every lifted edge crosses. I inspected the frozen scripts without running them. The second frozen script covers the affine incidence reconstruction, connectivity, nonbipartiteness and stabilizers, not metric recomputation on its own.

value.rationale: The vertices and local moves are the natural proper two-colorings and single-point changes of a small projective plane, not a slice selected by matching census numbers. Identifying this reconfiguration graph and its color-swap quotient as named symmetric graphs explains its exact transition geometry and relates a coloring question to independently developed graph theory. This remains useful even with the separate six-set classification and Foster metrics already known; re-enumerating those metrics alone would not pass.
